newsitem.title: USA: Calif. pension system names new investment officer.
newsitem.headline: Calif. pension system names new investment officer.

text.p: SACRAMENTO, Calif., May 11 - California's $68 billion State Teachers' Retirement System (CalSTRS) will replace its veteran chief investment officer with Patrick Mitchell following months of controversy over the fund's returns.

Mitchell, 48, has worked at CalSTRS since 1988 and currently serves as its director of fixed income and equities. He will replace Tom Flanigan, who has held the chief investment officer position for 11 years, CalSTRS said.

"Patrick Mitchell is an extremely talented investment professional and is highly regarded by the investment management community," said Emma Zink, the retirement board's chairperson. "The priority will be to continue the fund's long term growth and diversification in a prudent manner."
The CalSTRS shake-up, announced on Friday, was not a surprise. Top state finance officials have for months been critical of the pension fund's investment performance.

The CalSTRS fund was outperformed by the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) by over 300 basis points last year, according to a report by the state's controller. The 300 basis points represented $1.8 billion of earnings.

CalSTRS reported a 9.9 percent investment gain for the year ending December 31, versus the 12.9 percent of CalPERS, which is the largest public pension system in the United States with more than $100 billion in assets.

CalSTRS looked outside the organization for candidates to replace Flanigan. But James Mosman, CalSTRS chief executive officer, said, "It became apparent that Pat Mitchell possesses the unique skill set to carry the system into the next millennium."

To ensure an orderly transition, CalSTRS said Flanigan has been offered a contract to serve as a strategic investment consultant for at least one year. The terms of that arrangement have not been finalized, the retirement system said. Flanigan was not immediately available to comment on the offer.
Prior to joining CalSTRS, Mitchell had more than 10 years of experience as an asset-liability manager, controller and treasurer for three large West Coast financial institutions.
As chief investment officer, his base salary will be $185,000 to $230,000 with a 10 percent bonus incentive.

With assets of $68 billion, CalSTRS is the fourth largest public pension fund in the United States. Its members include over 540,000 active and retired California public school teachers, kindergarten through community college, and their beneficiaries.
